required_outcomes: Recognises the date conflict: R-5026 is booked with Keystone Compliance for Monday 12 October 10:00-12:00, the verified tenant cannot be in that day, and she says she agreed Monday 19 October 10:00-12:00 with engineer Isaac, which nothing from Keystone confirms.

Contacts Keystone Compliance now (before the 24-hour free-rebooking cut-off on Sunday 10:00): tells them nobody will be in on Monday 12 October so the slot should not go ahead, and asks them to confirm Monday 19 October 10:00-12:00 or offer another slot.
Tells Clara in writing (email, her preference) that Monday 12 October is being stood down and that 19 October is not confirmed until Keystone replies, and sets a dated follow-up to chase Keystone.
acceptable_alternatives: Keeping R-5026 on hold waiting for the provider (with a review date) instead of a separate follow-up, as long as Keystone and Clara are both contacted now.
positive_behaviours: Uses the verified spelling Hughes, not the speech-to-text 'Hedges', and treats the failed first verification as a mishearing.
Mentions that rebooking with more than 24 hours' notice avoids the £60 + VAT no-access charge.
red_flags: Records Monday 19 October as the booked visit on the tenant's word alone.
Tells Clara she is booked for 19 October as fact.
prohibited_actions: Telling Clara to be home on Monday 12 October, or leaving the 12 October slot standing with Keystone uninformed.
Escalating a routine rescheduling to a human.
critical_failures: Takes no action: neither Keystone nor the tenant is contacted, so Keystone attends an empty flat on Monday.
